quotes.quote: A goal must be present to have power.
quotes.why: This compresses the chapter's mechanism into a memorable, reusable line.

quotes.quote: The loudest want is not always the deepest want.
quotes.why: This plainly resolves the false assumption that temptation disproves a sincere long-term value.

quotes.quote: For the first half of this week, use your usual all-or-nothing rule. For the second half, swap in the Three-Power Check and compare which half made the next action clearer.
quotes.why: This asks readers to preserve a potentially harmful failure pattern for several days merely to create a comparison.

quotes.quote: That is why the three powers are not slogans.
quotes.why: The deep read refers to the three powers without defining them, so it depends on the fast read.

complaints.problem: The section invokes 'the three powers' without naming or defining I will, I won't, and I want, so it fails the stated stand-alone summary standard. Reserved category: STRUCTURALLY INVALID.
The section assumes the reader already knows the three-power framework and never gives a compact definition of all three roles, so it does not stand alone. Reserved category: STRUCTURALLY INVALID.

It directs readers to continue their usual all-or-nothing rule for half a week even though the chapter's examples include medication handling, spending, anger, and family care; deliberately preserving those defaults could cause avoidable harm. Reserved category: UNSAFE.
The phrase 'willpower's roots' asks about origins, while the prose demonstrates social uses and consequences rather than an evolutionary or historical origin.

Across most questions, the correct answer is the only qualified, mechanism-based choice, while distractors advertise themselves through absolutes such as 'only,' 'every,' 'must be fake,' and 'proves.'
The scenario stops at Brooklyn naming the goal and supplies no observed behavioral consequence, so it is a thin-but-usable illustration rather than a demonstrated before-to-after transfer case.
The phrase 'your first habit is to call every lapse weak refusal' is syntactically compressed and less immediately intelligible than the otherwise beginner-friendly chapter.
The repeated attribution of nearly every scenario to the same control model adds little new explanation and gives the section a templated rhythm.

parsedReview.oneParagraphVerdict: The chapter has a strong, memorable core move: distinguish starting, stopping, and remembering the larger value, then make the missing power visible at the choice point. Its concrete cues, compact lines, and prefrontal-control mechanism support retention and transfer, and the quiz answers are derivable. However, the distractors are often guessable without reading, Q5 overstates what the prose establishes, and the supposedly layered deep and full reads depend on an earlier definition instead of standing alone. Most importantly, the weekly comparison exercise tells readers to retain a known all-or-nothing failure pattern for half a week across domains that include medication, money, anger, and caregiving. That unsafe instruction and the broken stand-alone summary structure keep an otherwise capable chapter below the shipping bar.
